question: What will U.S. seasonally adjusted advance initial jobless claims be for the week ending September 12, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is a stable low-claims regime: last advance print 206k, 4-wk avg 207.25k, 2026 band 189-230k, with Challenger reporting the slowest layoff pace in four years. My prior comes from the late-Aug-to-mid-Sept 2-week change over 2015-2025 ex-2020, which was negative in 9 of 10 years with median -8k (residual seasonality), implying ~198k off a 206k base. I shrink that heavily to a ~204k median because 2026's Labor Day sits inside the target week rather than the prior one, seasonal factors are re-estimated annually, and street consensus for the intervening week is 209k. Two-sided evidence: downside from the seasonal dip and 2026's repeated below-consensus prints (Aug 1 came in 199k vs 203k expected); upside from TS Edouard's Sept 1 Louisiana landfall bleeding filings into the target week, though the comparable Arthur landfall in June left no national mark. I do not observe the Sept 5 print (released Sept 10), so this spans two weeks of unseen news. The Kalshi week-ending-Sept-5 ladder implies a ~204k median and 189-220k 10-90 — a one-week-off near-miss contract, used as corroboration rather than an anchor. Tails: sub-184.5k would be a 60-year low (3%); above 240.5k needs a +35k shock such as the Texas fraud surge that drove the Sept 6, 2025 print to 259k, or a major disaster, neither currently in view (1.5%).

- Advance-vs-revised: advance prints are typically revised UP by roughly 1-2k, so an advance figure sits slightly below the level the same week eventually settles at. The w/e Aug 22 figure was revised from an advance to 204,000.
- Extreme-print precedent within this class: w/e 2025-09-06 printed 259,000 against 236,000 the prior week, a +23k jump attributed to a fraudulent-filing surge concentrated in Texas, which unwound to 233k the following week. Source: FRED ICSA.

calls.reasoning: Last published advance figure is 206,000 for the week ending Aug 29, 2026 (4-week MA 207,250); the Sep 5 print lands Sep 10, after this run, so I am forecasting two weeks ahead from Aug 29 with no intervening observation. Level has been stable in the low-200s all summer (Jul 18 189k to Aug 29 206k, mean ~204k over the last 8 weeks), so status quo is a print near 205-210k and I centre at 207,000 with a small upward tilt: the week ending Sep 12 is the first full week after Labor Day (Mon Sep 7, 2026), a period where seasonal-adjustment factors historically add noise and where the last two Septembers printed above the August level. Dispersion, not direction, is the whole game here: the empirical 10-90 band of 2-week ICSA changes in 2026 is roughly -14k to +19k, so I use a ~31k 10-90 width, right-skewed because claims spike upward far more readily than they collapse downward. Escapes: below 184,500 needs a sub-2026-low print (2026 floor was 189k) — priced at 2%; above 240,500 needs a +35k jump, for which there is a concrete recent precedent (the Sep 2025 spike to ~263k driven by fraudulent filings concentrated in one state, plus hurricane-season and large-layoff mechanisms) — priced at 3%. Market check: the harness found no Polymarket or Manifold contract. Kalshi does run a weekly KXJOBLESSCLAIMS series and a market for this release almost certainly exists, but kalshi.com returned HTTP 429 on my fetch and search surfaced only older weeks (Feb/May/Jun 2026), so I have NO price to anchor on and did not blend one; treat this as 'market exists but price not retrieved'. Evidence is thin and one-sided in the sense that it is all just the recent level series, so I stay close to the reference-class anchor rather than manufacturing a view.

calls.reconciliation: Three disputes mattered. (1) FACTUAL, settled: Labor Day 2026 is Monday Sep 7, which falls inside the Sun Sep 6 - Sat Sep 12 reference week; Run 2's claim that this is a full post-holiday week is a calendar error, so its +207k tilt loses its stated basis and I do not average it in. (2) FACTUAL, partly settled without web access: Run 1 and Run 3 report different 2025 entries (-3k vs +30k) for the same-sounding class; this is a class-alignment difference (calendar-date week ending ~Sep 13 vs the Labor-Day-containing week ending Sep 6), not a data conflict. The Labor-Day-containing alignment is correct for 2026, and 2025's positive is attributable to the Texas fraudulent-filing surge; ex-event median is about -9k under either definition, so the anchor holds. (3) FACTUAL, reconciled as compatible: Run 1's TS Edouard upside and Run 3's NHC 'no formation next 7 days' are not in conflict - Edouard made landfall Sep 1 so its filings mostly hit the Sep 5 week, and the June Arthur landfall left no national mark, so I price the upside tail at the thinner end (1.5%) rather than Run 1's or Run 2's framing. JUDGMENT calls: dispersion, where I take the median of three independently computed SDs (11.7k x 2.56 = 30k) rather than the widest; and the degree of shrinkage from the 198k reference-class anchor, where I adopt Runs 1 and 3's reasoning that annually re-estimated seasonal factors absorb part of the residual, but land at 203k rather than 204k because the target is the advance print, which runs ~1k below the level the week eventually settles at. Could not settle from the dossiers: any economist consensus or live market price for the Sep 12 week - none exists in any run's retrieval, and the Kalshi KXJOBLESSCLAIMS ladder covers the Sep 5 week only (same instrument, wrong reference week), so it is corroboration at ~204k, never an anchor.
